column2: req_desc

Keycloak sign-in
Signing in goes through Keycloak with a fresh state and PKCE for every attempt, and the callback creates a session only once and only in the browser that started that attempt, as qualified in Server boundary.

Role-gated desks
Each desk page and each member or staff API answers only to the realm role that owns it, and every other signed-in role gets the 403 set out in API.

Bidder registration landing
A newly self-registered person who registers to bid lands on `/bidder`, which shows their pending limit status, and reloading or opening that address shows the same screen.

Spending-limit approval
The admin approves a pending bidder with a spending limit, which assigns the next paddle number, lets the bidder bid and sends them one notice.

Sign-in outage
While Keycloak is unreachable, signed-in people keep bidding and working their desks, and starting a sign-in answers 503 at once with the published outage banner.

Consignment intake landing
A consignor who submits a watch or camera lands on `/consign` with the new lot listed in its intake state, and reloading shows the same desk.

Empty consignor desk
A consignor with no lots sees the published empty desk wording on `/consign`.

Owner-only records
Bidders open only their own invoices and offers, and consignors only their own lots, offers and statements; any other id, even a guessed one, answers 404.

Consignor view without bidders
The consignor's lot views and socket frames show the price, bid count and result but never a paddle number or any other bidder detail.

Specialist estimate
The specialist sets the estimate, opening bid, hidden reserve, condition notes and portrait on an intake lot, validated as in API, which moves it to estimated.

Catalogue order and close times
The specialist orders estimated lots into a sale and publishes it, which numbers the lots and closes them one lot gap apart from the sale's end on the database server's time.

Lot state guards
Lots, sales, offers, invoices and statements move only along the state machines in Business rules, and each illegal move answers 409 and changes nothing.

Specialist desk layouts
The specialist desk shows its Intake, Estimate and Sale order regions in one, two or three columns, switching exactly at 768 and 1200 pixels of viewport width.

Pinned sale poster
The home page pins the current sale title over six procedural lot portraits with captions, the published bottom-left line and one gold action to the catalogue.

Catalogue complete on first load
The catalogue and each lot's bid history arrive complete in the first response, in closing-soonest order, together with the sequence number the page's socket resumes from.

Keyboard catalogue grid
A bidder moves through the catalogue grid with the arrow keys, Home and End, opens a lot with Enter, and keeps focus on the same lot when an extension reorders the grid.

Catalogue layouts
The catalogue shows one, two or three tile columns with the pinned title above or beside them, switching exactly at 768 and 1200 pixels of viewport width.

Phone browsing
At 375 pixels wide the home, catalogue and lot pages never scroll sideways and every control is at least 44 by 44 pixels.

Published increment table
Every lot's next bid is its current price plus the increment the published table gives for that price.

Maximum bidding
The leader pays one increment over the second-highest maximum but never more than their own, equal maximums go to the earlier bid, and raising your own lead never raises the price, as qualified in Business rules.

Reserve rule
When a maximum reaches the hidden reserve, the price jumps to the reserve, and the lot reports the reserve met from that moment only.

Spending limit under concurrency
A bid is refused if it would take the bidder's leading maximums on open lots past their spending limit, and of two bids sent together that would pass it between them exactly one is accepted.

One bid per key
Bids sent together or retried with one idempotency key count as one bid and one history row and all get the original response, and the same key with a different body answers 409.

Keyboard bid form
A bidder picks the bid type in a radiogroup, types a maximum and confirms in a dialog that keeps Tab inside it and closes on Escape, with focus returning to Place bid.

Draft maximum survives
A typed but unsent maximum survives reload, Back and a second tab on the same lot, and neither the per-second countdown nor live updates clear it or the last bid message.

Bidder-safe fields
Every bidder-facing and public response and socket frame carries only the published fields: other bidders as paddle numbers, your own maximum only, and never the reserve.

Place a maximum
An approved bidder signs in, opens a lot from the catalogue, places a maximum and sees the confirmed price, the lead and the new history row without reloading.

Per-lot soft close
A bid accepted inside a lot's soft-close window moves only that lot's close to one window after the bid, and no other lot's close moves.

Close edge on server time
A bid the database server checks before the lot's close counts, and one checked at or after the close answers 409 with the lot's result.

Server-decided lot status
The lot page and catalogue show a lot open, closing or closed exactly as the server reports it, whatever time the device clock shows.

Bid removal recompute
The admin removes a bid and the server at once recomputes the price and leader from the remaining bids, keeping any extension that bid caused.

Live recompute on every open view
Every open bidder, public and consignor view of a lot shows a new price, a removal, an extension or a close in place within one second, with no reload.

One socket with replay
Each page opens exactly one live socket, sends no bid until it is open, and after a drop receives every event after the last sequence it saw, once each.

Connection-lost banner
While a page's socket is down it shows the published banner with a gold retry link, and removes it once the socket is open again and has replayed.

Lot close outcomes
Within one second after a lot's close the server decides sold or unsold from the bids and the reserve, and the public result never changes afterwards.

Announced lot events
Every page has a hidden polite status region from first paint that announces each price change, reserve met, lot close and notice once, in the published words.

One notice per recipient
Each timed or decided event writes exactly one in-app notice per recipient with the published text, listed newest first for that person.

Watched-lot notice
A watched lot sends each watcher one closing-soon notice ahead of its current close, moved if an extension arrives before it goes out.

Win a lot
A bidder who leads at the close sees the lot page turn to sold, hears the win announced and finds the lot under Won on their dashboard.

Second-chance offer
For a lot that closed unsold with bids, the consignor may once offer it to the top bidder at an amount from the final price up to that bidder's maximum, open for the offer window.

Offer expiry edge
Second-chance and default offers can be accepted only before their expiry by the server's time, and an accept at or after it answers 409.

Second-chance choice
The consignor answers the second-chance choice on their lot page, the top bidder accepts the offer from their dashboard, and the consignor sees the lot sold by offer.

One invoice per buyer per sale
When a sale's last lot closes, each winning bidder gets one invoice holding every lot they won by hammer in that sale, and each accepted offer gets its own invoice.

Premium and VAT
Each invoice line carries the hammer, the tiered buyer's premium and VAT on the premium only, each rounded half up to the cent, as set out in Business rules.

Payments at the cashier
The cashier records payments against an invoice before its due time, the invoice turns paid when nothing is outstanding, and overpayments and late payments are refused.

Cashier settles an invoice
The cashier opens a buyer's invoice on the cashier desk, records the full payment, and the bidder's invoice page then shows it paid.

Default at the due time
An invoice unpaid at its due time defaults, and each hammer lot on it is offered to its underbidder at the underbidder's maximum for the offer window.

One outcome per lot
A lot is never won twice: hammer, second-chance and default offers exclude each other, and two accepts of one offer sent together succeed exactly once.

Underbidder takes a defaulted lot
After a default the cashier sees it under Defaults, the underbidder accepts the offer from their dashboard, and the lot is invoiced to them.

Seller commission
Each sold lot on a seller statement carries the seller commission with its per-lot minimum, rounded half up to the cent, as set out in Business rules.

Locked and superseding statements
An issued statement never changes, and a correction issues a new statement that supersedes the old one and links to it.

Consignor reads a statement
The admin issues a consignor's statement and the consignor opens it from their desk at its own address, set as a printed sale result.

Hammer Numeral
When the server confirms a new price, only the changed digits of the pinned price roll, right to left, the next-bid line updates, and the time left counts up after an extension.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion requested, the price digits, the time left and the poster swap change instantly to their end state, with the same announcements.

Saleroom look
Every screen carries the warm black ground, Anton for the sale title, price and document headings, Work Sans with lined-up figures for every amount, and one gold action.

Legible price on every ground
The large price on the lot page stays readable over each of the six procedural portrait grounds.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port and answers the health check.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never written into source and never sent to the browser.

Server boundary
The server accepts state-changing requests and sockets from its own origin only, enforces the published body limits and never serves source files or credentials.

Desk state in the address
A desk's chosen filter is part of its address, so reloading it, going Back to it or opening it in a second tab shows the same filter checked and the same rows.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build` and `serve` and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and nothing else is needed to start the app.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` at `/app` lists every shipped package with its licence. Shipped packages are the Go modules the program imports and the front end's production dependency tree (`npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`), plus the two font families.
Every shipped package uses MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, ISC or MPL-2.0. Fonts use OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are the provided PostgreSQL and Keycloak. No other database, cache, queue or file-based state store is used.
The provided service configuration (the compose files and the seeded realm and client settings) is left untouched.
The page loads no script, style or font from any third-party origin at runtime.
`go.sum` and `package-lock.json` are committed and match the dependencies in use.
